stem: Section 22 of RA 9003 requires waste containers to be marked "compostable," "non-recyclable," "recyclable" or "special waste." Which item belongs in the special waste container?
hints: Special waste needs extra care because it can harm people or the environment.
Section 3(pp) of RA 9003 defines special wastes as "household hazardous wastes" and gives examples.
Sort each choice: does it rot (compostable), is it on the list of recyclables in Section 3(z), or is it hazardous (special)? Only one choice is hazardous.

solution.methodName: Match the term to its legal definition

steps.action: Recall Section 3(pp): special wastes are "household hazardous wastes such as paints, thinners, household batteries, lead-acid batteries, spray canisters and the like."
steps.why: Hazardous means it can harm health or the environment if it is handled the wrong way.

steps.action: Sort the other choices. Vegetable peelings rot, so they are compostable. Newspaper and tin cans are both listed as recyclable materials in Section 3(z).
Only household batteries appear in the list of special wastes.
The answer is used household batteries.

trapNotes.Vegetable peelings: Peelings rot and can become compost. They go in the compostable container.
trapNotes.Old newspapers: Section 3(z) lists newspaper as a recyclable material. It goes in the recyclable container.
trapNotes.Empty tin cans: Section 3(z) lists tin cans as a recyclable material. They go in the recyclable container.
